name: Single-Org vs. Multi-Org Comparison Matrix
description: 8-dimension comparison of single-org vs. multi-org Salesforce architecture for pharma/life sciences. Use during customer workshops to support the org strategy recommendation.

pros: Shared data model with unified Customer 360
Single source of truth for HCP/Account data
cons: Complex sharing rules to enforce data boundaries
PII from different LOBs coexists — security configuration critical
Data model becomes complex and controversial as scope grows

pros: Simpler sharing model within each org
Independent data model evolution per org
cons: Requires MDM/data warehouse for consolidated view

pros: Standard processes enforced across all LOBs
Single release calendar for process changes
Collaboration between LOBs with shared account lists
cons: Hard to run different process speeds for different LOBs

pros: Faster speed to market for individual LOBs
Pooled API and storage limits across all users
Single set of limits to manage and monitor
cons: All LOBs compete for shared limits
Hard limits cannot be purchased away

pros: Fresh set of limits per org
LOB growth doesn't impact other orgs
cons: Total cost of limits higher (base allocations per org)
Must monitor limits across all orgs
Governance overhead scales with LOB count
Org-wide settings become hard to govern
Data residency may not be achievable

pros: Real-time data access across all entities
cons: Performance impact of large report volumes

pros: No cross-LOB data leakage in reports
cons: Higher infrastructure cost for unified view

pros: Deploy changes once for all LOBs
cons: All LOBs on same release cadence
Environment management more complex with more profiles

pros: LOBs can move at their own speed
cons: Deploy changes N times across N orgs
Full sandbox refresh limited to 1/month per org
Higher governance and architectural complexity cost
More expensive failure impact (all LOBs affected)
